newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open 0.05 cent weaker Thursday, dealers said, on follow-through selling from the previous session.
The May contract expired on a weak note Wednesday, ending down 0.18 cent at 11.14 cents a lb after trading from 11.45 to 10.95 cents.
Most-active July settled off 0.07 cent at 10.96 cents after ranging from 11.09 to 10.92 cents. The back months closed 0.03 to 0.09 weaker.
Volume was estimated to have reached 32,430 lots.
May/July spread settled at 0.18 compared with 0.29 on Tuesday's close, after July traded at a slight premium to May briefly during the session.
Merrill Lynch said in a daily comment that "expectations for close to 400,000 tonnes of sugar being delivered were borne out with 6,799 lots believed to be delivered, mostly from Brazil."
The large quantitiy to be taken off the board could eventually weigh on the July contract, analysts said.

LIFFE white sugar futures were trading lower on Thursday following losses in New York and in response to ample availability of sugar in the near term, traders said. At 0845 EDT/1345 GMT, August stood 1.40 weaker at $309.00, while the back months were 20 cents to 70 cents weaker.
((-- S Rostler New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
